project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Develop and demonstrate systems that recover industrial excess heat and convert it to mechanical or electrical power.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Develop and validate new ways to recover and convert excess industrial heat to mechanical or electrical power. Demonstrate the technology in operating factories and consider adding storage.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Factories need options to recover heat that would otherwise be lost. Power production from waste heat and storage could also help offset higher electricity use as factories electrify.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Provide a working industrial demonstrator, standardised components and open guidance for plant control systems. Develop business models for using the recovered heat, including flexible electricity production where relevant.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Demonstrate measurable gains in energy efficiency, economic performance and safety. Where the project makes electricity, quantify its flexibility and expected grid value.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Survey factories’ needs before designing the solution, standardise suitable components and share the results. Provide open guidance usable by other plants in the same sector.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The proposal needs at least three independent funded partners in three different eligible countries. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: The industrial team needs a working factory, heat recovery and conversion expertise, and participants able to integrate the system with existing controls.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer: The plant team must be able to carry out a physical demonstration in an operating factory. Identify wider sector needs before design and build integration guidance that other plants can use.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on industrial waste heat to power and represent it to the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate the project if it can develop grid-facing flexibility evidence or requirements for the flexible-generation business model. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder). The plan must include an operational industrial site and a credible plant team.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could develop grid-facing flexibility evidence or requirements for the flexible-generation business model as an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant). It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could develop grid-facing flexibility evidence or requirements for the flexible-generation business model. Budget at least 30% of those costs from other resources. The rate helps set a lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending). The topic explicitly covers flexible-generation business models. A partner focused on network analysis needs a substantive task tied to that work.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could define the operating characteristics that make recovered-heat generation useful for the grid. A credible funded contribution would need to support the flexible-generation business model or its evidence.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: Develop a novel recovery and conversion system. The industrial demonstration must show a credible improvement over available solutions.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Innovation covers heat recovery and conversion equipment, integration with industrial processes and standardised components that other factories can use.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Identify factory requirements before design, develop and validate the system, then demonstrate it physically in an operating industrial site.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 7–8 (technology readiness level: from a prototype demonstrated in operation to a complete, qualified system) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Specific conditions

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Use one or more operating industrial sites for the physical demonstration. Check that the equipment can work with existing plant control and energy management systems.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Integrate the system with industrial processes and usable supplies of excess heat, with storage where appropriate. Standardise common components to make it transferable to similar factories.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Demonstrate measurable improvements in recovering and converting waste heat. Show how the same sector can use the results, with open technical and economic guidance.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: Identify the needs of factories in the target sector before designing the system. Demonstrate it in one or more operating industrial sites.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer: Assess reliability, safety and physical and cyber protection as part of the measured results. The integration plan should cover the host’s industrial control environment.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Specific conditions

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 13.5 million for industrial waste heat to power. It expects 2 awards.
- Grant request: around EUR 6.75 million per project. Different requests remain eligible.
- Funding form: Lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · p. 45 · Overview of this call
Demonstration of industrial excess/waste heat conversion to mechanical or electrical power · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards industrial waste heat to power. The rate is used to set the lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 207–209 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Plan the budget for industrial waste heat to power using the cost categories allowed by the grant. Use estimates to set the fixed grant.
- Budget detail: Set out the main cost categories by beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and work package (separately planned blocks of project work).
- Purchases and subcontracting: Apply best-value and conflict-of-interest rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Lump Sum Funding in Horizon Europe: What do I need to know? · pp. 6–7, 26–27 · Detailed budget table

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for industrial waste heat to power around acceptance of completed blocks of work.
- Payment model: Pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant), then periodic payments for accepted work packages (separately planned blocks of project work) and a final balance.
- Retention or guarantee: 5–8% of the maximum grant is deducted from pre-financing for mutual insurance.
- Financial reporting or audit: Keep evidence of implementation and completion.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 33 · Reporting & payment arrangements
Lump Sum Funding in Horizon Europe: What do I need to know? · pp. 17–23 · Payment schedule, Reporting and payment, Keeping records

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for industrial waste heat to power through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 15 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. The technical proposal (Part B) is limited to 45 pages.
- Opening: 5 May 2027.
cards.sources:

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for industrial waste heat to power.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting industrial waste heat to power is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around 5 months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): Around 8 months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Conditions before starting: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) must conclude a written consortium agreement (the partners’ written agreement on how the project will run).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
Use the portal’s forms to submit the proposal and supporting documents for industrial waste heat to power.
- Application form: Complete Part A in the Portal and attach Part B and mandatory annexes.
- Registration: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to funded partners) need participant identification codes (organisation registration numbers).
- Partner documents: The coordinator confirms its authority to act for the applicant group.
- Budget: Provide the detailed lump-sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending) budget table with the full proposal.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 4–5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Industrial waste heat to power proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Full proposal: Excellence, impact and implementation are scored. Each criterion needs 3/5 and the total needs 10/15.
- Impact is weighted by 1.5 in Innovation Action (a grant for developing and demonstrating new solutions) full-proposal ranking.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The industrial heat-to-power call can restrict transfer of ownership or sole rights to use results.
- Conditional requirement: Provide standardised, cost-competitive components and open integration tools.
- Conditional requirement: Screen beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work) control and use the specified European Union services for covered satellite data or services.
- Exception — Transfer of results: The granting authority may object to a transfer of ownership or to exclusive licensing (giving another party sole rights to use the results) for up to four years after the project ends.
